title: Sampling Playground — Decoding a Toy Next-Word Model
description: A clearly labelled toy next-word model — a hand-written table of scores for each word given the previous word — for exploring how decoding works: temperature, top-k, top-p (nucleus), repetition penalty, and greedy versus sampling. Two columns of settings sit side by side, each with a bar chart of the raw and adjusted distributions, a correctly computed entropy readout, word-by-word stepping, and five seeded whole-sentence runs.
prompt: Build 'Sampling Playground': a clearly labelled toy next-token model, meaning a small hand-built distribution over words given the previous word, so people can explore decoding. Include temperature, top-k, top-p (nucleus), repetition penalty, and greedy versus sampling. Show a bar chart of the adjusted distribution, an entropy readout (computed correctly), seeded sampling of whole sentences, and side-by-side runs with two settings. Make it obvious that this isn't any real model, and state the order the steps are applied in. Give it a typewriter-and-paper feel.

methodology: Independent numeric oracle: the spec recomputes softmax at a given temperature from the documented start-of-sentence scores and compares every bar's exact probability (data-p) to 9 decimal places.
Entropy checked against the displayed probabilities with −Σ p log₂ p, plus the derived 2^H 'equally likely choices' and the raw-model entropy.
Metamorphic checks on temperature: entropy rises monotonically from 0.3 to 1 to 2, never exceeds log₂ of the vocabulary size for that context, and is exactly 0 at T = 0 (greedy).
Filter semantics: top-k leaves exactly k non-zero words, and top-p leaves exactly the smallest prefix of the sorted distribution whose mass reaches p, each renormalised to 1.
Determinism: two columns with copied settings produce identical five-sentence runs, a reload reproduces them, and greedy decoding yields one distinct sentence.
risks: Floating-point cumulative sums making top-p drop a word it should keep (an epsilon is used at the cut-off).
Softmax overflow at low temperatures (scores are shifted by their max before exponentiating).
Repetition penalty applied to the wrong tokens or with the wrong sign for negative scores.
People mistaking the toy for a real model; the label is on the page header, footer and meta.
qa.playwright: Range sliders are driven with locator.fill(), which Playwright supports for input type=range and which fires the input event the page listens to. Every bar carries its exact probability in data-p, so the spec can do real arithmetic (softmax, entropy, nucleus) instead of parsing rounded percentages. Randomness is a mulberry32 PRNG seeded from ?seed=, and the most robust determinism check compares two columns against each other rather than against hard-coded sentences, except for greedy where the output is fully determined by the table.
coverage: Exact probabilities at T = 0.7, sum to 1, entropy, perplexity and raw entropy readouts
Temperature monotonicity, the uniform upper bound, T = 0 greedy
Top-k = 2 renormalisation and cut words, top-p = 0.7 nucleus
Forcing words, repetition penalty effect, finishing and clearing a sentence
Copied settings match, reload reproducibility, greedy runs identical

a11y: All knobs are labelled range inputs with visible values, decoding mode is a pressed-state button group, and each bar is a button whose label reads the word, its raw and adjusted probability and whether it was filtered out. The growing sentence is a polite live region, so stepping is announced.
